resources.string:
Chronicle is a Baylor College of Medicine research data-collection app for one approved study enrollment per installation. Before collection begins, the app identifies the study and its HTTPS server, shows the requested data types, and records consent choices.

This Google Play release may collect app package names and labels, app foreground/background and timing events, an optional in-app activity-class name, device lifecycle events, battery and charging state, connectivity state, selected device settings, upload-delivery diagnostics, and whether the device user selects study participant or someone else after unlock. Research records are encrypted on the device and uploaded over authenticated HTTPS only to the enrolled study server.

When an upload fails, Chronicle keeps a bounded aggregate containing the affected upload family, closed failure category and count, first and last occurrence, HTTP status when available, and bounded exception class. After connectivity recovers, it is sent under the active participant/device enrollment and retained by the server for no more than 30 days. The diagnostic record contains no server URL, free-form error text, invitation secret, API key, authorization token, password, or stack trace.

This release does not collect Health Connect or other health records, activity or sleep recognition, continuous hardware-sensor measurements, audio or media metadata, notification content or metadata, accessibility interactions, physical location, contacts, messages, typed text, websites, searches, screenshots, photos, videos, microphone recordings, crash logs, advertising identifiers, financial information, or advertising profiles. It contains no advertising or cross-app tracking SDK.

To withdraw from Chronicle collection, uninstall the app. Uninstalling stops future collection and Android removes Chronicle's on-device app data. The Play app has no in-app withdrawal or server-deletion control, and an uninstall cannot notify the enrolled study server. Questions about participation or records already uploaded must go to the research team identified in the study consent.

Baylor College of Medicine compliance information is available at https://www.bcm.edu/about-us/our-campus/compliance. Application support: uzairalam998@gmail.com.

Chronicle requests Usage Access only for app-usage data you accepted. It records app package names, open and close times, foreground duration, and—when configured—an in-app activity class name. These research records are encrypted on this device and uploaded to the enrolled study server shown during enrollment. Chronicle does not collect content inside apps, typed text, messages, websites, search terms. You can decline by leaving this screen or revoke access later.

If you continue and enable Chronicle in Android Usage Access settings, Chronicle can record app package names, open and close times, foreground duration, and—when configured by your study—an in-app activity class name. These research records are encrypted on this device and uploaded to the enrolled study server shown during enrollment. Chronicle does not collect content inside apps, typed text, messages, websites, search terms. You can cancel now or revoke access later.
